regional.syndrome: Lifelong asymptomatic carriage in over 90%. Adult T-cell leukaemia/lymphoma (ATL) appears after a latency of forty to sixty years, usually in those infected through breastfeeding, with a lifetime risk of a few per cent; HTLV-1-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis (HAM/TSP) in under 4%, presenting as spastic paraparesis with bladder dysfunction. regional.headline: The first human retrovirus discovered, infecting 5-10 million people. Most carry it for life without consequence; a minority develop adult T-cell leukaemia/lymphoma after decades, or a progressive myelopathy.

regional.geography: Sharply defined endemic foci rather than a global distribution: south-western Japan, the Caribbean, parts of South America, West and Central Africa, Iran, Romania, and Aboriginal communities of central Australia, where some adult seroprevalences exceed 40%.
